faqs.question: What does LoloBuy do?
faqs.answer: LoloBuy acts as a purchasing agent: you provide a seller listing, select the item, pay for the purchase and Chinese domestic delivery, then review the warehouse stage before arranging international shipping. The seller supplies the goods. A product link or spreadsheet entry is a starting point for checking an order, not confirmation of current stock.

faqs.question: How do I order through LoloBuy?
faqs.answer: Paste the original product link into LoloBuy, check the imported listing and select the exact color, size and quantity. Review the item price, domestic delivery and any requested services before payment. LoloBuy’s official guide then separates purchasing, warehouse inspection and international parcel submission into distinct stages.

faqs.question: What if LoloBuy cannot read my product link?
faqs.answer: The official buying guide describes a manual shopping-agent order form when automatic import is unavailable. Complete the actual product information and chosen options, and review the order before submitting it. Do not replace a marketplace item ID with a spreadsheet’s internal page number: they identify different records.

faqs.question: Can several items share one Chinese delivery fee?
faqs.answer: LoloBuy’s domestic-delivery FAQ describes one charge when products from the same seller are submitted and checked out together. An unusually large or heavy order can require an additional delivery payment. This arrangement does not automatically combine charges across different sellers or include international shipping.

faqs.question: How do I ask LoloBuy to apply a seller’s discount?
faqs.answer: Record the real promotion or free-domestic-shipping offer in the order remarks so the purchasing agent can verify it with the seller. The official help also describes using Order Enquiry if the promotion information was omitted. A claimed discount must be checked; a spreadsheet cannot promise that an old offer still applies.

faqs.question: Can I change my size or color after ordering?
faqs.answer: Before the seller dispatches the item, LoloBuy says it can negotiate a change. After dispatch, the help page describes a possible warehouse return followed by a new order instead, with return delivery costs. Send the request against the actual order promptly and wait for acceptance before assuming the option has changed.

faqs.question: What does Pending for Confirmation mean?
faqs.answer: Some order details need your confirmation. Read and answer the message attached to the order. Official help directs purchased-order questions to Shopping Agent Order and warehouse-stage questions to My Warehouse, where an accept-or-return decision may be requested. Menu wording can vary; waiting for a tracking update does not answer the request.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Received and In Stock?
faqs.answer: The official status guide uses Received when the warehouse has signed for the seller’s parcel and inspection is underway. In Stock means the quality check is complete and the items are stored in your inventory. Warehouse receipt therefore does not mean your QC review or international shipment is already finished.

faqs.question: What does standard QC check?
faqs.answer: LoloBuy’s standard inspection checks visible order details such as style, quantity, color, size, model and obvious damage. Read the actual inspection service and your order photos together. A visual check is not a guarantee of authenticity, precise fit or long-term durability.

faqs.question: Are sealed items and electronics fully tested?
faqs.answer: No. The inspection rules describe exceptions for sealed products and explicitly exclude authenticity, function and quality testing for professional electronics and related goods. With the no-inspection option, the warehouse checks restrictions but does not verify the product or provide QC photos. Review the chosen service before relying on an inspection result.

faqs.question: Can I request more QC photos?
faqs.answer: The service overview describes additional photos on request; the photo-service page also offers Secondary Quality Inspection when inspection was skipped before storage. The official pages give differing standard photo counts. Check your selected service and request the specific missing view or measurement, rather than assuming every order includes the same number of images.

faqs.question: How long can items stay in the LoloBuy warehouse?
faqs.answer: The dedicated storage page and current status guide state 180 days for ordinary stored goods, while an older buying guide still says 90. Abnormal unmatched parcels have separate rules. Check the deadline displayed for your own item and arrange shipping or any extension before it expires; do not rely on the older guide alone.

faqs.question: Can I ship several purchases in one parcel?
faqs.answer: The buying guide describes selecting stored items in My Warehouse and submitting them for delivery together. Check that all chosen items have completed the necessary review and that the available route accepts the resulting parcel. Combining items changes the packed parcel; it does not guarantee a lower total freight charge.

faqs.question: Can LoloBuy remove boxes before shipping?
faqs.answer: The Package Removal service can be selected when submitting delivery. Its official description says necessary protective packaging is retained. If you need original boxes for a gift, storage or a possible return, consider that before choosing removal. The final packing result and freight depend on the goods and chosen shipment.

faqs.question: Why can the final shipping charge differ from the estimate?
faqs.answer: The initial freight is based on estimated weight and the chosen destination and route. Packing can change weight and dimensions, and the logistics provider’s charge determines settlement. LoloBuy describes refunding overpayments or requesting a supplemental payment when the actual freight differs. Check the final parcel quote and account message.

faqs.question: What is volumetric weight?
faqs.answer: It converts the parcel’s dimensions into a weight used for billing bulky goods. LoloBuy’s help distinguishes route-specific formulas and notes that billable weight can be the greater of actual and volumetric weight. Use the divisor and rounding rules shown for your selected route, not a universal price-per-kilogram claim.

faqs.question: What should I do about an extra shipping-payment notice?
faqs.answer: Open the corresponding parcel and review the revised charge and confirmation request. LoloBuy’s supplemental-payment rules use different handling thresholds and include cases where a parcel can be held or canceled. Respond to the deadline shown for your parcel and settle any accepted balance; do not treat the original estimate as final.

faqs.question: Where can I track my international parcel?
faqs.answer: The official buying guide directs users to My LoloBuy → Parcels after dispatch. The status guide distinguishes Packed from Shipped: a packed parcel may still await final weight confirmation, while Shipped means it has a tracking number and has been handed to the carrier. Read the latest carrier event as well as the account status.

faqs.question: Can I cancel an order before it reaches the warehouse?
faqs.answer: Cancellation depends on the current order stage. Use the relevant order’s cancellation or return/refund option. Once the item has been purchased, seller confirmation may be required; a submitted request is not an approved refund. Check the response in that order before making a replacement purchase.

faqs.question: What does LoloBuy’s five-day return rule cover?
faqs.answer: The dedicated rule describes a 120-hour request window starting at the next hour after Stocked in for eligible goods. Seller agreement, item condition and required packaging still apply. A no-fault return can involve both domestic shipping legs and a handling fee. Check eligibility and the actual request page promptly.

faqs.question: Where is an approved refund sent?
faqs.answer: The return-help page generally describes crediting approved refunds to the LoloBuy account balance. It separately describes a narrow original-payment-method exception for certain PayPal orders awaiting approval. This is not a promise that every refund goes straight to a bank card, or evidence that every payment method is currently available.

faqs.question: What should I do if my delivered parcel is damaged or wrong?
faqs.answer: Open the affected parcel in My LoloBuy → Parcels and use Apply After-sales. Describe the issue and retain clear photos of the parcel and product. The official article contains conflicting claim windows, including an earlier warning, so report the problem immediately and obtain case-specific confirmation rather than waiting for a generic deadline.

faqs.question: How should I choose a clothing or shoe size?
faqs.answer: LoloBuy’s size reference warns that store standards can differ. Compare the actual seller’s measurement chart, units and chosen option with your measurements or a well-fitting item. Its conversion tables are references, not a guarantee that one label fits across every seller. Ask about missing measurements before ordering.

faqs.question: Do 1688 orders use the same purchase and inspection rules?
faqs.answer: The official 1688 guide requires the seller’s minimum quantity; prices and domestic freight can vary with quantity. Inspection rules distinguish sampled Type A products from Type B products without standard QC. Confirm the quantity, inspection scope and return terms before payment instead of assuming retail-order treatment.

articles.title: How to use a LoloBuy spreadsheet: turn a product link into a useful shortlist
articles.description: Find products by category, compare the exact listing and keep the details you need before opening an item on LoloBuy.
articles.summary: A useful spreadsheet helps you narrow the search. A useful shortlist records the exact item, option and unanswered questions you will need for the order.

sections.heading: Start with a buying decision, not a long list
paragraphs: A LoloBuy spreadsheet is a product discovery tool. You can browse a category, look at product images and follow a listing to the next step. It does not mean that the catalogue publisher has purchased every item, tested the seller or reserved your chosen size. Treat each row as a lead that needs checking.

Before searching, write down the type of item you need, the measurements that matter and an approximate item budget. Searching for a black zip hoodie is more useful than collecting every attractive clothing link. A narrower question also makes it easier to recognise when a listing is missing essential information.

sections.heading: Keep the original product identity
paragraphs: The number in a catalogue page address may be a local record number. It can differ from the marketplace product ID used in the purchase link. Do not change the numbers by hand to make a link look right. Use the matching product button, then compare the item that opens with the listing you intended to buy.

Save the original seller URL with your chosen option. A screenshot can preserve a useful view, but it is less useful if you cannot tell which seller, size or colour it belongs to. If a link opens a different product or an empty listing, pause and check it before proceeding.

sections.heading: Compare like with like
paragraphs: A starting price can apply to the least expensive option, a single accessory or a different quantity. Compare the same item configuration across listings. A two-piece set and a single top are not a meaningful price comparison, even when their thumbnail images look similar.

Check whether the gallery shows the selected colour and whether a size chart exists. Identical photographs across sellers do not establish identical construction or stock. Your comparison should record the evidence that is present and leave a visible gap where something important is unknown.

sections.heading: Use the official buying handoff
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s buying guide describes submitting a marketplace link, selecting the available options and paying for the item and domestic delivery. It also describes a manual order form when product information cannot be captured automatically. Opening a link successfully is therefore only the start of the order review.

On the official product page, check the image, option text and quantity again. A catalogue cannot guarantee current stock or preserve a choice that you have not selected in the checkout. Keep any special requirement specific enough for a buyer to act on, such as the exact colour name or a measurement question.

sections.heading: Separate discovery photos from your own QC
paragraphs: A seller gallery explains the offer. A historical warehouse image can show someone else’s item. The inspection images attached to your own order are the evidence to review before sending that item overseas. These three image types answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable.

Your shortlist should travel with the order. When the item reaches the warehouse, compare the recorded option with the visible size tag, colour and quantity. A mismatch is easier to explain when you have the original selection and order reference together.

sections.heading: Make the shortlist useful after purchase
paragraphs: Keep only the strongest candidates and record why each survived the comparison. For example, one hoodie may have a clearer measurement chart while another has an unresolved fabric detail. This turns a collection of links into a decision you can revisit without starting the research again.

Before buying, read the ordering and budget guides. Before parcel submission, read the QC and shipping guides. The spreadsheet is most useful when it connects those stages rather than presenting an item price as the complete cost of a delivered order.

checklist: Save the exact source URL and option.
Compare matching quantities and configurations.
Resolve missing measurements before payment.
Check the imported listing on LoloBuy.
Review order-specific QC before shipping.

articles.title: How to order on LoloBuy: product links, options and payment stages
articles.description: Follow the ordering process from a marketplace link to warehouse inspection and a separately submitted international parcel.
articles.summary: Check the item before payment, the warehouse evidence before shipping, and the parcel quote before dispatch. Each stage answers a different question.

sections.heading: Begin on the official site
paragraphs: Use the official LoloBuy website for registration, account access and payment. This independent catalogue helps with discovery; it does not collect your account password or process your order. Check the destination when opening a product and keep purchase conversations attached to the relevant order.

The official buying guide describes starting with a product link from a supported Chinese marketplace. The item you select is supplied by the seller behind that listing. That distinction matters because a purchasing service and a seller do not control the same parts of the transaction.

sections.heading: Check the imported product
paragraphs: Paste the original product link or use the catalogue’s matching LoloBuy button. Compare the resulting page with the source before selecting options. Check the main image, item name, seller information where available, selected colour, size and quantity. Do not rely on the image alone.

If the page presents a manual shopping-agent form, the official guide says to enter the order information manually. Fill it from the actual listing rather than guessing missing options. When a required detail is unclear, clarify it through the order enquiry process before asking the buyer to proceed.
bullets: Option text matches the intended colour and size
Quantity and unit price refer to the same configuration
Any special requirement is written clearly

sections.heading: Understand the first payment
paragraphs: The official purchase workflow separates the item and Chinese domestic delivery from the later international parcel. Review the first payment line by line. Selecting a destination during purchase does not mean that the displayed item total includes every charge needed to deliver the goods to that destination.

Payment methods, currencies and optional services should be checked in the current checkout. A help article’s general list is not a promise that every method is available for your account or order. Save the payment record and compare it with the order status rather than paying again because a page refresh feels slow.

sections.heading: Respond to order questions
paragraphs: LoloBuy has a “Pending for Confirmation” status for information that needs to be verified. Its help page directs the buyer to the instructions on the order. Read the actual question and reply to that issue: it could affect whether the purchasing team can continue.

The official modification guidance distinguishes items the seller has not dispatched from items already sent. Before dispatch, the buyer can ask the seller about a change; after dispatch, a return and new order may be needed. A requested change is not a completed change until the order record confirms it.

sections.heading: Review arrival and inspection
paragraphs: Warehouse arrival and completed inspection are separate milestones. Find the item in the warehouse area and compare the photos and recorded option with your purchase. Check identity first, then the visible details that matter to you. Resolve an obvious mismatch before including the item in an international parcel.

Do not assume all products receive the same inspection. The official standard-inspection policy describes limits for sealed products and special handling for some 1688 orders. If you need a particular measurement or view, check whether it is available for your order rather than treating a general QC image as proof of everything.

sections.heading: Submit the parcel as its own decision
paragraphs: The official workflow instructs users to select stored items, enter delivery details and choose from the available shipping options. Review the destination, restrictions, packing choices and freight deposit together. An item that has been bought is not automatically an international parcel ready for dispatch.

The final freight can differ after packing and logistics measurement. Watch the parcel record for any adjustment or confirmation request. Once dispatched, use the parcel section for tracking, keep the order references and check the contents promptly when the delivery arrives.

sections.heading: Build a first-order record you can reuse
paragraphs: Before submitting a first order, prepare a compact record with the seller URL, item title, exact option, quantity, size-chart reference and unanswered questions. Keep the seller's original option wording when a translation could be ambiguous. For a set, identify the components expected in the package. This record provides a comparison at checkout and later at the warehouse, rather than relying on a remembered thumbnail.

For illustration, a clothing order might specify one navy sweatshirt in the seller's size M, with a particular flat chest measurement shown on the chart. That is a clearer instruction than asking for a medium blue top. If the chart or colour name is unclear, ask before purchasing. A precise request improves communication but does not establish that the seller has the item in stock or that the garment will fit.

sections.heading: Separate a product problem from a payment problem
paragraphs: If the imported item is incorrect or a required option is absent, resolve the listing before paying. Use the original source to identify whether the seller changed the offer or whether the import omitted information. A manual order, when offered, should preserve the actual product details. Changing IDs or selecting an approximately similar option does not resolve an uncertain order and can make a later mismatch harder to document.

If the item is correct but payment status is unclear, compare the bill, account balance and payment-provider record. Preserve the transaction reference and visible error before trying again. A loading page does not by itself prove failure. Ask support to clarify an ambiguous debit rather than creating several overlapping attempts. Keep product identity, payment status and seller dispatch as separate checkpoints because success at one stage does not establish success at the next.

sections.heading: Plan a warehouse decision before parcel submission
paragraphs: Decide which evidence you need before the goods arrive. A size-sensitive garment may require a specific measurement, while an accessory set may require a clear view of all components. Check the available inspection service and its limits. When the photos are ready, compare them with the saved order record and list each unresolved detail. Request a particular view or explanation rather than a general judgement that the item looks good.

Check the relevant return conditions promptly while the goods remain in the warehouse. Storage time and the seller's return window are different deadlines. Waiting to combine several items can leave an unwanted item outside its applicable return period. If you want a replacement or return, ask about that item's eligibility and expected costs before moving it into an international parcel. Do not assume a parcel can be stopped after every later processing step.

sections.heading: Finish the order with a complete cost record
paragraphs: Keep goods and domestic delivery, selected services, international freight and destination charges in separate fields. Add a charge only once and record its currency. Replace estimates with confirmed bills as the order progresses, retaining the earlier figures for comparison. If freight changes after packing, match the adjustment to the parcel reference and measurements. That record explains the delivered cost more clearly than a single undated total.

After delivery, compare the received contents with the original item list and preserve packaging evidence if there is a problem. Use the relevant order or parcel support route, describing the issue and the records that connect it to your purchase. Retain the dates of purchase, warehouse arrival, dispatch and delivery as separate milestones. These observations can inform your next order without becoming a promise that another parcel will follow the same timing.

Before closing the record, identify which steps required clarification and which assumptions changed. If a product link needed manual entry, keep the confirmed option text for future reference. If the freight estimate changed, keep the measured carton beside the original estimate. These notes should describe your own order only. Recheck the current listing, checkout and shipping conditions when ordering again, even when the item appears identical. A previous successful purchase does not reserve stock or preserve the same price, service or seller terms.

checklist: Confirm the original product and exact option.
Review item and domestic-delivery charges.
Answer pending confirmation requests.
Check your warehouse photos and unresolved issues.
Review the separate international parcel quote.

articles.title: LoloBuy QC photos: a practical inspection checklist before shipping
articles.description: Separate seller photos from your own warehouse inspection and check identity, visible condition and the details that still need evidence.
articles.summary: Start with the item and option you ordered. Then use the available views to decide what is clear, what needs another photo and what should be resolved before dispatch.

sections.heading: Identify the evidence you are looking at
paragraphs: A product gallery is part of the seller’s offer. A reference QC photo may show an earlier order. Your own warehouse photos relate to the item received for your purchase. Keep those categories separate when making a decision, especially when a product has several colours, versions or sizes.

Begin by matching the order reference, product and selected option. A detailed photo of the wrong version is not useful reassurance. If the image set cannot be connected to the item in your warehouse, ask for that connection before judging its appearance.

sections.heading: Check identity before small details
paragraphs: Review size, colour, quantity and model first. Look for consistent labels and views of the same item. A photo set can be attractive while still showing the wrong size tag or an incomplete set. Compare what you see with your saved order selection instead of relying on memory.

For a pair of shoes, check both shoes and the visible size markings. For a garment, check the selected colour and labelled size. For a bag or accessory set, check that the expected components are visible. These are practical review steps, not a guarantee that every hidden detail has been inspected.

sections.heading: Use a category-specific checklist
paragraphs: For clothing, useful views include the overall shape, front and back, seams, print or embroidery and any area where the fit depends on a measurement. For footwear, inspect the pair together, visible construction and the requested size. For bags, closures, handles and interior views can answer different questions.

Write down only the details that influence your decision. A long generic list can distract from the one missing measurement or damaged closure that matters. If the front view is clear but the back is missing, ask for the missing view rather than another general photo of the same angle.
bullets: List missing views separately from observed defects

sections.heading: Understand the standard service limits
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s standard-inspection page describes appearance checks and exclusions. In particular, sealed items are not always opened, and certain professional or electronic products are not checked for authenticity, function or quality. Some 1688 orders follow sampling or different inspection rules.

The official pages do not agree on a single universal photo allowance: the inspection page and broader service page describe different counts. Check the service attached to your order instead of assuming an exact number. The useful question is whether the available evidence covers the issue you need to decide.

sections.heading: Ask for a specific additional view
paragraphs: A focused request identifies the order, the area to photograph and the reason. For example: “Please show the size label and measure the garment’s flat chest width from seam to seam.” That is clearer than asking whether the item is good. Check any service availability or charge before requesting extra work.

Use the same measurement method as the seller’s chart. Flat garment width and body circumference are different quantities. Keep the picture and measurement together so that a number cannot be mistaken for a measurement of another size or another item.

sections.heading: Make a documented decision
paragraphs: Sort findings into confirmed, unclear and unacceptable. If a detail is unclear, request evidence. If the item appears to differ from the order, use the relevant support or return process before international shipping. Keep a short description of the issue and the photos that demonstrate it.

Photos cannot establish every material property, comfort, long-term durability or internal function. Approving visible condition is a narrower decision. Read the return conditions while the item is still in the warehouse, and do not treat successful QC as a promise about customs or international delivery.

sections.heading: Turn a clothing check into a clear request
paragraphs: Start with the measurements that influence fit rather than asking the warehouse to judge whether a garment is the right size for you. For a sweatshirt, you might need flat chest width, body length and sleeve length measured from the same points as the seller's chart. State the measurement method and unit. A size label is useful identity evidence, but it does not replace the garment measurements.

If the chart uses body circumference while the photograph shows flat width, do not compare the two numbers directly. Check where the tape starts and finishes, whether the garment is laid flat and whether the number can be read. Lighting and perspective can also change how a colour looks. Where colour matters, ask for a clearer view, while recognising that a screen photograph cannot guarantee an exact real-world shade.

sections.heading: Inspect shoes and accessories without overclaiming
paragraphs: For footwear, compare both shoes, visible size markings, the overall shape and the areas relevant to your concern. If a particular measurement or close view is needed, identify it explicitly. For a bag, check handles, closures and expected components where visible. For a multi-part accessory, make a list of what should be included and compare that with the photographs instead of assuming a closed box contains everything.

A visible seam or surface defect can be documented with a close photograph and its location. Hidden construction, comfort during use, material composition and long-term durability usually require different evidence. Do not treat a warehouse photo as an authenticity certificate or a professional functional test. For sealed products or specialist electronics, read the stated inspection exclusions before deciding whether the available service answers your actual concern.

sections.heading: Keep uncertainty separate from a confirmed defect
paragraphs: Use three simple states in your notes: confirmed match, needs more evidence, and observed mismatch. For example, an unreadable size label belongs in the second state until a clearer photograph is available; a clearly different size label belongs in the third. This prevents a missing photograph from being described as a proven defect, and prevents an attractive overall image from hiding an unanswered question.

For each unresolved point, record the order number, relevant image, precise question and next action. When a response arrives, update that point rather than replacing the whole record with a vague approval. If a mismatch remains, ask about the applicable remedy while the item is still at the warehouse. Keep the seller's acceptance, return requirements and any charges together. Requesting a return is not the same as having one approved.

sections.heading: Make the decision before the next deadline
paragraphs: Review the item promptly when its warehouse information becomes available. LoloBuy's return guidance makes eligibility conditional on the order, seller and timing. A general storage allowance does not extend a return window. Read the deadline and condition requirements applicable to the item, and preserve original packaging when it may be needed. Do not delay a necessary enquiry merely because other items in a planned parcel have not arrived.

When you approve an item for shipping, record what was actually checked and what remains unknown. For example, identity and visible measurements may be confirmed while comfort and durability remain untested. Keep that limited conclusion attached to the item reference. Revisit any unresolved concern before parcel submission, particularly if a packing change would remove labels or original packaging relevant to the record. This creates a useful decision trail without pretending that QC eliminates every purchase risk.

Keep the original images and a short decision note together rather than saving only a cropped detail. The wider image helps connect the concern to the correct item, and the order reference connects the photograph to your purchase. If another image later resolves the question, retain both and state what changed. Avoid sharing personal order information publicly. The useful record is a specific observation with a traceable source, not an unsupported rating or a claim that every product from the seller has been checked.

checklist: Match the photos to your own order.
Verify size, colour, model and quantity first.
Ask for the specific missing view or measurement.
Check the inspection service and its exclusions.
Resolve significant issues before parcel submission.

articles.title: LoloBuy shipping costs: calculator, weight and fees
articles.description: Use the LoloBuy shipping calculator, compare actual and volumetric weight, and check packing choices, freight adjustments and the complete parcel budget.
articles.summary: A useful freight comparison starts with one clearly defined parcel. This guide explains the inputs and checks; it is not a live shipping quotation.

sections.heading: Separate the item price from freight
paragraphs: The price beside a product is not the complete delivered cost. The official LoloBuy workflow separates purchasing the item and domestic delivery from paying the international shipping deposit later. You can estimate a budget before buying, but you cannot make a final parcel comparison from the product price alone.

Write down the destination, intended contents and the packaging you expect to keep. A pair of shoes with its box and the same pair without it are different packing decisions. Extra items can change both weight and dimensions, so adding one small purchase may affect the final quote in more than one way.

sections.heading: Know which weight you are comparing
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s weight guide distinguishes an estimate from the packed parcel’s real weight. The warehouse item record includes original packaging, while the final parcel also involves the outer shipping package and any removal or reinforcement choices. These stages can produce different measurements.

Volumetric weight reflects the space occupied by the package. The official guide publishes different calculation divisors for different routes. Do not apply one divisor to every carrier or assume an old example is today’s tariff. Use the current route conditions for the parcel you are submitting.
bullets: Route-specific billing rules and included services

sections.heading: Use arithmetic without pretending it is a quote
paragraphs: For illustration only, a parcel measuring 40 × 30 × 20 centimetres has a volume of 24,000 cubic centimetres. A hypothetical route using a divisor of 6,000 produces 4 kilograms of volumetric weight; a divisor of 5,000 produces 4.8 kilograms. Neither calculation supplies a shipping price.

The example shows why the route rule matters. You still need the actual weight, billing increments, destination and current rate. Avoid choosing a route from a headline “per kilogram” claim when the charge depends on a first unit, additional units or a larger chargeable weight.

sections.heading: Compare the same parcel across routes
paragraphs: Keep the inputs fixed while comparing available lines. Check which contents are accepted, the stated transit estimate, tracking, packaging requirements and any optional protection. A lower initial amount is not a complete comparison if the services or restrictions differ.

Treat delivery estimates as estimates. Warehouse handling, carrier movement and destination processes are separate stages. This guide does not promise a universal delivery time, a tax-free route or a fixed customs charge. Use the current quote and the destination’s official rules when making the decision.

sections.heading: Review packaging as a trade-off
paragraphs: The official package-removal page describes removing unnecessary outer packaging while retaining protection needed for the goods. It also advises against selecting removal when original packaging matters for gifts or preservation. Reducing volume can be useful, but protection and the purpose of the purchase still matter.

Ask for a specific packing choice rather than a blanket instruction to remove everything. Compare the final measurements if available. Consolidation or packaging removal does not automatically produce a lower bill on every route, and an easily damaged item may need more protection instead.

sections.heading: Watch the final settlement
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s supplemental-payment guidance says that estimated freight is reconciled with the logistics provider’s actual charge. This can mean a refund of overpayment or an additional payment request. Read the parcel messages and respond to any request attached to your shipment.

Keep the initial estimate, final chargeable measurements, selected services and adjustment together. That record makes a difference easier to understand. Budget possible destination charges separately and check the final parcel total before treating the order as complete.

sections.heading: Use the official calculator with a saved baseline
paragraphs: Open LoloBuy's current shipping estimator and select the actual destination. Enter the requested contents, weight and dimensions using the displayed units. Save the date, input values, selected service and currency with the result. If the goods have not reached the warehouse, label the measurements as estimates. That label matters because a seller's approximate item weight does not describe a finished carton with its outer packing.

Record one baseline before changing a packing option or removing an item. For each alternative, change one variable and retain the others where possible. If a route disappears when the goods category changes, that restriction is part of the result; selecting an inaccurate category to obtain a cheaper quote does not make the route suitable. Compare only services offered for the actual goods and destination, and keep any unanswered eligibility question visible.

sections.heading: Build a comparison that includes every parcel
paragraphs: Use one row for each complete shipping scenario. Record the contents, number of parcels, actual weight, dimensions, packing services, route and total freight. For a two-parcel option, add both complete parcel quotations before comparing it with one combined shipment. Separate minimum charges can affect the result. A lower number for the first parcel alone does not show that splitting the whole order is cheaper.

A meaningful comparison also records protection and service differences. One scenario may preserve a shoe box while another removes it; one may include reinforcement that another omits. Write down those changes so that the amount does not hide a different outcome. If the final measurements are unavailable, treat the comparison as planning evidence and repeat it after packing information is confirmed. Do not convert an estimated saving into a guaranteed final bill.

sections.heading: Audit a changed estimate line by line
paragraphs: If the final freight differs from your saved estimate, first compare destination, selected items, actual weight and carton dimensions. Then check the route, billing increment, optional services and currency. A heavier outer box, a bulky item or a different service can explain a change even when the product list appears similar. Ask for the specific measurement or line item that changed instead of assuming that every difference represents the same fee.

Keep the initial deposit and any later adjustment linked to the same parcel reference. An account credit for overpayment and a refund to an external payment method are different records. Confirm where the amount was credited or what supplemental payment remains due. If the explanation is incomplete, preserve the two quotations and ask an order-specific question. This is more useful than comparing your total with an unrelated parcel from another destination or date.

sections.heading: Keep freight separate from the delivered budget
paragraphs: The international freight figure may not include every payment associated with receiving the goods. Review the original item purchase, domestic delivery, optional warehouse work, payment charges and destination costs separately. Mark an included service clearly to avoid counting it twice. A blank amount should remain a question to resolve, rather than silently becoming zero in a delivered-cost estimate.

Before paying, check current destination information and the selected service's stated inclusions. Do not infer customs treatment or buyer protection from a route nickname. If you later publish a shipping example, include the date, contents, destination, measured carton and scope of the quoted amount, removing personal information. A well-documented historical case can help readers reproduce the comparison, while an isolated price cannot establish the rate for their own parcel.

A comparison worksheet can remain simple: one line per scenario, with the quotation date, destination, goods, weight source, dimensions, route, amount and unresolved questions. Add a final column for the confirmed result when the parcel is dispatched. Do not replace the original estimate without keeping its inputs, because that would remove the explanation for the difference. If an input remains unknown, obtain it from the current parcel record or support before making a firm comparison. Use this method for each new parcel rather than extending one historical price to every future purchase.

checklist: Compare routes for identical contents and destination.
Check actual and volumetric weight rules.
Keep packaging protection in the decision.
Separate estimates from final charges.
Read parcel adjustment messages before dispatch.

articles.title: LoloBuy warehouse guide: inspection, storage and consolidation
articles.description: Organise stored items, resolve QC questions and choose packaging with the complete parcel in mind.
articles.summary: The warehouse stage is your chance to connect the purchase record with the received item and decide what is ready to ship together.

sections.heading: Distinguish arrival from readiness
paragraphs: A seller’s delivery scan means a domestic package has reached a point in its journey. It does not by itself show that your item is inspected, correctly matched and ready for international dispatch. LoloBuy’s status guide separates received goods, inspection and stored inventory.

Use the warehouse record rather than a single tracking message as your working list. Keep the order number, selected option and QC status for each item. If several seller packages arrive together, this prevents one completed item from hiding a question about another.

sections.heading: Build a small warehouse checklist
paragraphs: For each item, record what you ordered, what the warehouse shows and what remains unresolved. This can be as simple as four columns: item, correct option, inspection decision and packing instruction. The point is to keep a pending question visible before you assemble a parcel.

Review the images against the original selection. A missing photo and a visible defect require different actions. For an unclear detail, ask for the relevant evidence. For an apparent mismatch, explain the difference with the order reference and consider the applicable return process.
bullets: Ready for international parcel: yes or no

sections.heading: Check your storage deadline directly
paragraphs: The official material contains conflicting storage statements: the buying guide mentions 90 days, while the storage and status pages mention 180 days. The storage page also describes separate treatment for unmatched abnormal packages. These differences should not be reduced to one unconditional promise.

Check the storage information attached to your own item and clarify any discrepancy before relying on a deadline. Record the date and any paid extension you choose. Do not leave goods waiting indefinitely because a general article gives a longer period than the current warehouse record.

sections.heading: Consolidate compatible, resolved items
paragraphs: The official buying guide describes selecting stored items for an international delivery or buying more and sending items together later. Consolidation lets you plan the parcel as a whole. It does not make every combination acceptable for every route.

Before combining items, consider restrictions, fragility and unresolved issues. An item waiting for a return decision should not be treated as ready. A delicate accessory may need a different protection choice from clothing. Compare the eventual parcel dimensions and weight, not just the number of products.

sections.heading: Write precise packaging instructions
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s package-removal help describes removing unnecessary packaging while preserving protection that the product needs. If you want original packaging for a gift or collection, leave removal unselected and make the requirement clear. The value of a box is not always its shipping weight.

Use item-specific instructions where needed: keep a fragile item’s protective support, retain one retail box, or ask which packing choice is available. Review any extra service charge in the current parcel form. Do not assume that the same packaging approach fits every category.

sections.heading: Do a final parcel review
paragraphs: Confirm the item list, quantities, recipient details, selected route and services before submission. Check that all intended items are included and nothing with an unresolved issue has slipped into the parcel. This short review is easier than trying to reconstruct the choice after packing.

The official weight and freight-settlement pages explain that final measurements can change the charge. Keep an eye on parcel messages after submission, including requests for confirmation or additional payment. Once dispatched, use the parcel tracking record and keep the warehouse evidence until the delivery has been checked.

checklist: Review every item before marking it ready.
Check the deadline shown for your own storage record.
Keep return questions separate from shipping-ready items.
Specify packaging choices that fit each product.
Review the final parcel list and freight adjustments.

articles.title: LoloBuy size guide: compare measurements before choosing a label
articles.description: Use the seller’s chart, consistent measurement methods and targeted warehouse photos to make a clearer sizing decision.
articles.summary: A familiar size label is a starting point. The useful comparison is between the seller’s measurements, your reference measurements and the fit you want.

sections.heading: Start with the seller’s chart
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s official size reference says that sizing standards can vary between stores and treats its conversion information as a reference. A label such as medium or a familiar shoe size does not establish how every seller’s product will fit. Read the chart for the exact listing and option.

Check whether the numbers describe a body, a finished garment or a recommended wearer. Those are different measurements. If the chart does not make this clear, ask before ordering instead of choosing a larger or smaller size by habit.

sections.heading: Measure a reliable reference
paragraphs: For clothing, compare against a garment you own that fits in the way you want. Place it flat and use the same points as the seller’s diagram. Note the units and whether a width is measured across one side or around the body. Keep the measurements with a quick photo of the method.

For body measurements, follow the relevant guide and keep the tape level rather than tightening it to force a preferred size. A fitted shirt, a relaxed hoodie and a structured jacket need different allowances. The desired silhouette is part of the decision, not a defect in the chart.

sections.heading: Choose the dimensions that matter
paragraphs: For a top, chest width, body length, shoulder and sleeve can answer different fit questions. For trousers, check waist, rise, inseam and overall length. A single waist number does not explain how a trouser leg will sit, and a chest measurement alone does not establish sleeve length.

For illustration, suppose your reference top measures 56 centimetres across the chest and 70 centimetres in length. A candidate measuring 56 and 64 may have similar width but a noticeably shorter body. This is an example of comparison method, not a recommendation for a particular size or product.
bullets: Match body measurements to body charts
Match flat garment measurements to garment charts
Compare more than one fit-critical dimension
Record the intended relaxed or fitted silhouette

sections.heading: Check footwear separately
paragraphs: The official size guide recommends using the larger foot when the two differ and notes that length labels do not fully describe width. Read the seller’s footwear chart and check the system used on the selected option. Do not assume that an EU, US or UK number transfers perfectly between every listing.

Measure as the chart instructs and consider socks, width and the intended use. A visible shoe label in a warehouse photo can help confirm what was sent, but it cannot establish how the shoe feels on your foot. Avoid treating an insole photo as a universal conversion table.

sections.heading: Use QC to answer a specific question
paragraphs: Before shipping, compare the visible size tag with the order. If an important garment dimension remains uncertain, request that measurement using clear start and end points. For example, ask for flat chest width measured seam to seam rather than simply “check the size.”

LoloBuy’s inspection policy has limits and does not promise a full fit assessment. Check whether the measurement or additional photo is available for your item and whether there is a charge. A standard photo set should not be described as a personalised sizing consultation.

sections.heading: Decide while options remain open
paragraphs: If the received label differs from the selected option, document the mismatch using both the order and the photo. If the label matches but the measurement is unsuitable, check the seller’s return conditions and current order process promptly. These are different situations and should be described accurately.

Measurements reduce uncertainty; they do not remove differences in cut, stretch, fabric feel or personal preference. Keep the chart and your comparison notes so that a successful fit can inform a future purchase. Recheck the actual listing when ordering again, because another seller or version may use different measurements.

checklist: Use the exact listing’s chart.
Keep units and measurement methods consistent.
Compare several fit-critical dimensions.
Check the received size label and requested measurement.
Resolve fit questions before international dispatch.

articles.title: LoloBuy tracking: distinguish the order from the international parcel
articles.description: Read purchase, warehouse and parcel stages correctly, and collect useful evidence when a tracking update is unclear.
articles.summary: An order status and a carrier scan describe different parts of the journey. Keep the item, domestic package and international parcel references separate.

sections.heading: Know what you are tracking
paragraphs: A product can have a purchasing order, a seller’s domestic shipment and a later international parcel. These are related records, but they are not the same shipment. A domestic delivery message can mean arrival at the warehouse rather than delivery to your home.

Create a simple reference list when the order progresses: product/order number, seller tracking reference if shown, warehouse item record and international parcel number. This makes it easier to ask about the correct stage without sending support a screenshot that refers to a different journey.

sections.heading: Read the purchase stages first
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s official status guide distinguishes awaiting payment, processing, ordered and shipped by the seller. Processing concerns the purchase workflow; it does not mean that an international carrier is moving your parcel. Read the status wording before looking for an overseas tracking update.

The same guide describes received goods and inventory after inspection. If the domestic carrier says delivered but the warehouse inspection is not complete, those records can describe consecutive stages rather than a contradiction. Check the item record and any confirmation request for the next required action.

sections.heading: Then read the parcel stages
paragraphs: After you create an international parcel, its status has its own sequence. The official page describes waiting for payment, processing, packed and shipped. It also tells users to watch for freight changes after final weighing. A created parcel should not be mistaken for a dispatched parcel.

Use the actual record rather than the existence of a reference number alone. A label or number can be prepared before the next visible carrier movement. When comparing systems, note which page says the package has been handed over and which event the carrier has actually recorded.

sections.heading: Interpret quiet periods carefully
paragraphs: A gap between scans does not identify the cause by itself. Check the selected route’s current estimate, the last recorded event and any official notice relevant to that route. Do not turn a typical duration from an old post into a promised deadline for your parcel.

Avoid repeatedly opening different tracking sites and treating every wording difference as a new event. Keep a dated record of meaningful changes. If the current stage appears inconsistent or an action is requested, raise that specific issue through the parcel or order support channel.

sections.heading: Send a useful support question
paragraphs: Provide the order or parcel identifier, the tracking number, the last visible event and the question you need answered. For example: “The parcel record says shipped, but the carrier has not shown a handover event. Can you confirm the handover status?” This is more actionable than “Where is everything?”

LoloBuy’s buying guide points users to the parcel area for tracking after dispatch. Use the enquiry connected with the affected record where possible. Do not include unrelated account details or payment credentials in a message about a tracking event.

sections.heading: Keep evidence through delivery
paragraphs: When the parcel arrives, check the outer condition and contents promptly. Retain the packaging, label and clear photos if an item is wrong, missing or damaged. Match the received items with the final parcel list rather than an earlier shortlist that may include products you did not ship.

The official parcel after-sales page asks for a detailed description and photos where an item is wrong or damaged, but its deadline statements conflict. Act promptly and verify the applicable deadline in the live support process. Do not wait because a general guide seems to offer a longer period.

checklist: Separate domestic and international references.
Check whether the parcel is created, packed or dispatched.
Read the last event with its timestamp.
Send support a specific, documented question.
Check delivery promptly and retain relevant evidence.

articles.title: LoloBuy returns and refunds: act at the right order stage
articles.description: Prepare evidence, check seller eligibility and understand the difference between cancelling an order, returning an item and a parcel claim.
articles.summary: A return decision depends on the item, seller and current order stage. Clear evidence and a prompt request are more useful than assuming one rule applies to every purchase.

sections.heading: Identify the process you need
paragraphs: Cancelling an unpurchased order, returning an item held in the warehouse and reporting a problem after international delivery are different processes. Start by checking the current order or parcel status. The relevant button and information may depend on how far the transaction has progressed.

LoloBuy’s cancellation and return pages describe several status-dependent steps and seller involvement. A request is not the same as approval. Read the response attached to your order and keep track of what has been accepted, what is pending and what action is still needed from you.

sections.heading: Preserve the exact evidence
paragraphs: Keep the item URL, selected option, order confirmation and relevant photos together. If the concern is the wrong size tag, show the ordered option and the received tag. If the concern is damage, show a clear overall view and a close view of the affected area. Describe what differs without exaggerating.

For example, “Ordered blue in size L; warehouse photo shows a black size M label” identifies a checkable mismatch. “Poor quality” is much less precise. If the photos are too unclear to establish the problem, ask for the missing evidence before deciding which remedy to request.
bullets: Requested remedy: clarify, cancel, return or exchange

sections.heading: Read eligibility and timing together
paragraphs: The official return-guarantee page describes eligibility conditions and a request window after stock-in. It also says seller agreement is required. Other help pages use different or awkward wording about timing. Check the deadline and service available on the actual order, and submit the concern promptly.

Packaging and resale condition can matter. Do not instruct removal of packaging that you may need for an eligible return before you understand the conditions. Used products, special orders and other categories may have different rules; a general promise of unconditional returns would be misleading.

sections.heading: Ask which costs apply
paragraphs: The return-guarantee guidance distinguishes the reason for the return and discusses domestic transport and service charges. A seller’s original free-delivery offer does not necessarily make a later return free. Ask for the costs relevant to your specific request before agreeing to proceed.

Keep the response in the order record. Clarify whether the amount includes transport back to the seller, any original domestic delivery charge and a service fee. A platform handling allowance and the seller’s shipping charges are different things and should not be combined into a vague “free return” claim.

sections.heading: Follow the refund destination and status
paragraphs: The official return guidance generally describes approved refunds going to the LoloBuy account balance, with a specific exception discussed for certain original-payment situations. Account credit and money returned to an external payment method are different outcomes. Check which applies before assuming the funds will appear in your bank account.

Seller approval, returned-item receipt and refund completion can be separate milestones. Keep the returned parcel reference if one is provided. When asking about a delay, identify the last completed step instead of starting a new request that omits the existing return record.

sections.heading: Handle delivered-parcel problems separately
paragraphs: For problems after delivery, the official instructions point to the affected parcel’s after-sales application and request a detailed description and photos. Keep outer packaging and the parcel label as well as product images. These help connect the damage or mismatch to the shipment.

That official page contains conflicting deadline statements. Report a problem promptly and obtain the applicable time limit directly from the current process. This guide does not promise approval, a universal refund time or compensation for every type of loss.

checklist: Check the current order or parcel stage.
Document the exact mismatch or damage.
Confirm eligibility, deadline and packaging conditions.
Ask about all applicable return costs.
Track approval and the actual refund destination.

articles.title: LoloBuy order budget: look beyond the product price
articles.description: Separate item costs, domestic delivery, optional services, currency conversion and international freight before committing to an order.
articles.summary: A useful budget separates confirmed amounts from estimates. Keep the product purchase and the later parcel payment visible as two connected decisions.

sections.heading: Price the option you will actually buy
paragraphs: A catalogue price is a starting point for comparison. The selected colour, size, set or quantity may have a different current price in the official order page. Review the exact configuration before using it in a budget, particularly when the source listing shows a range.

Compare the amount and currency at the same stage. A recorded item price, a checkout total and a card statement may include different components. Do not label their difference a hidden fee until you have checked quantity, delivery, conversion and any selected service.

sections.heading: Separate the two main payment stages
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s official buying process first collects payment for the items and Chinese domestic delivery. International freight is handled when the stored goods are submitted as a parcel. A buyer who budgets only the first payment can reach the warehouse stage without enough money to send the order.

Create a simple table with each cost component and mark it as confirmed or estimated. Keep optional services visible rather than hiding them inside the product figure. Possible destination charges belong in their own line because they are not established by the catalogue price.
bullets: Payment or currency-conversion charges shown at checkout
Potential destination taxes or handling charges

sections.heading: Read domestic-delivery conditions
paragraphs: The official domestic-delivery help says that items from one seller submitted and checked out together can share a domestic charge, with a possible additional balance for an overweight shipment. This is a specific condition, not a promise that all products in a cart share one fee.

Check which seller supplies each item and how the order is grouped. A larger quantity can also change the seller’s price or shipping terms, particularly for wholesale listings. Keep the current order calculation rather than dividing a previous delivery charge across unrelated purchases.

sections.heading: Check payment and currency details
paragraphs: Review the methods available in the official checkout, the currency being charged and any displayed costs before confirming. Availability can depend on the account and transaction. A general help-page list is not enough to establish that a particular method will be offered for your order today.

If a payment provider offers currency conversion, compare the final charged amount and terms shown there. Keep the receipt with the order. Do not promise a fixed exchange rate or assume that a previous purchase’s conversion will apply to the next one.

sections.heading: Treat discounts as something to verify
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s promotion guidance describes providing the seller’s offer details in the order remarks so the buyer can verify them. A banner or a saved screenshot is not proof that your exact option and quantity still qualify. Record the conditions and ask for confirmation through the order process.

Keep a discount separate from the ordinary budget until it is confirmed. Avoid relying on a referral promotion, coupon or shipping claim copied from an unrelated guide. This website has not supplied a guaranteed new-user credit or a universal shipping price.

sections.heading: Use a range for uncertain freight
paragraphs: Before packing, weight and size are estimates. The official freight-settlement policy reconciles the initial shipping amount with the logistics provider’s actual charge. Leave room for a possible adjustment instead of spending the entire budget on products.

As a planning exercise, suppose your confirmed items and domestic delivery total 100 units in one currency, while your current shipping estimate is 30–45 units. Your provisional total is 130–145 before other applicable costs. These are hypothetical numbers illustrating the method, not LoloBuy prices or a quote.

sections.heading: Make the budget a decision tool
paragraphs: If the likely total exceeds your limit, revise the shortlist before payment. Removing a low-priority item can be easier than trying to recover the money through a later return. Compare the value of the complete delivered order rather than the number of inexpensive products you can collect.

After dispatch, replace estimates with the final recorded charges. Keep the difference and its explanation. That history is useful for future planning, while still allowing for different goods, dimensions, routes and exchange conditions next time.

checklist: Budget the exact selected option.
Separate domestic and international delivery.
Record optional services and charged currency.
Use only confirmed discounts.
Keep a reserve for uncertain freight and destination costs.

articles.title: LoloBuy finds and reviews: check the evidence behind a listing
articles.description: Evaluate source details, review relevance and inspection limits without treating a badge, photo or rating as a guarantee.
articles.summary: The useful question is what the available evidence establishes about this transaction. A platform name alone cannot answer every question about a seller, product or parcel.

sections.heading: Separate the platform from the product
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s service information describes purchasing goods from third-party platforms rather than selling every listed item itself. This independent spreadsheet is another step removed: it organises discovery. Keep those roles clear when deciding who can answer a question or resolve a problem.

A working product link does not demonstrate authenticity, stock, fit or future delivery. Likewise, a complaint about one seller does not establish the cause of every platform issue. Start with the exact claim you need to evaluate and the party responsible for that part of the process.

sections.heading: Check a listing before checking its popularity
paragraphs: Look for a clear original URL, a consistent product description, identifiable options and useful size or specification information. Compare the selected option with the gallery. A cheap starting price can refer to a different component from the item shown in the main image.

If several sellers use the same photographs, those images alone cannot tell you whether the goods are made or supplied identically. Record what is missing and ask a focused question. A popularity number or a familiar batch name is not a substitute for evidence about the exact listing.
bullets: Unanswered questions that affect the purchase

sections.heading: Read reviews for relevance
paragraphs: A review is more useful when you can identify its date, the product or service discussed and the evidence behind the conclusion. A comment about support response time is different from a review of footwear fit. A parcel arriving successfully does not prove that every product in a catalogue is suitable.

Look for disclosed referral links, incentives or other relationships. Their presence does not automatically make a review false, but it helps explain its purpose. Do not turn an affiliate promotion, a single anecdote or an unverified testimonial into a universal recommendation.

sections.heading: Plan what inspection can establish
paragraphs: The official standard-inspection page describes appearance checks and important exclusions. It does not promise to authenticate or function-test every category. Sealed goods and some professional products receive different treatment. Read those limits before buying an item whose value depends on something the service will not test.

For a garment, clear measurements and visible construction may answer much of your question. For electronics or safety-related goods, a photograph cannot establish internal performance or compliance. If the necessary evidence is unavailable, that uncertainty belongs in the purchase decision.

sections.heading: Keep payment and communication in the right place
paragraphs: Use the official site for checkout and the relevant order or parcel enquiry for transaction questions. Check the domain before signing in. This catalogue does not need your password, payment credentials or a private conversation copied into a product search box.

Keep records of the chosen option, payment, seller clarification and any agreed requirement. If something changes, ask for the update in the order record. A clear history makes a later question easier to resolve than scattered messages that omit the item or transaction reference.

sections.heading: Make a decision you can explain
paragraphs: Write a short note covering why the item meets your needs, what evidence supports that view, the total budget and the uncertainties you accept. If the decision depends on an unanswered question about size, condition or return eligibility, resolve it before paying.

A small first order can be an optional way to limit the amount committed while learning a workflow, but it does not certify every seller or future shipment. This guide is a method for evaluating evidence, not a personal test report or a guarantee that LoloBuy is risk-free. Use the ordering, QC and returns guides for the next concrete checks.

checklist: Distinguish catalogue, platform and seller roles.
Check the exact listing rather than its popularity.
Read reviews for date, relevance and incentives.
Understand what inspection will not verify.
Keep a documented decision and order record.

articles.title: LoloBuy shipping to the Netherlands: costs, timing and parcel checks
articles.description: Plan a LoloBuy parcel for the Netherlands: compare calculator inputs, packing, delivery stages and the records needed to check import charges.
articles.summary: Use the Netherlands as the actual destination when comparing freight. Keep a dated quotation, distinguish delivery stages and check current Dutch Customs guidance before paying.

sections.heading: Start with a Netherlands parcel brief
paragraphs: A useful LoloBuy shipping comparison starts with the parcel you intend to receive, rather than a price someone else paid. Write down the destination country, postcode, item list, quantities and any packaging that must stay with the goods. A route available for a small clothing parcel may not accept a different mix of products. The country alone does not establish that your parcel is eligible.

Make two lists: facts already confirmed and information still estimated. Seller dimensions, warehouse item weight and the dimensions of a finished carton are different records. Mark their sources so that you know what to update after the goods arrive. If a gift box must remain intact, say so before comparing a cheaper packing option that assumes its removal. That choice can affect both protection and volume.

sections.heading: Read the price in separate stages
paragraphs: LoloBuy's official buying guide separates the first item payment and Chinese domestic delivery from a later international parcel submission. For a Netherlands order, keep these stages separate in your budget. The catalogue price is a starting point for the item, not a quotation for arrival at your door. Add only costs that the current order or parcel record actually confirms.

Keep a simple ledger with columns for the item, domestic delivery, optional warehouse services, international freight, payment costs and destination charges. Record the currency beside every amount. When a quotation already includes a charge, mark it as included instead of adding it again. An unanswered field should remain unresolved. A total with an explicit gap is more useful than a deceptively precise total that assumes every missing cost is zero.

sections.heading: Prepare a repeatable calculator comparison
paragraphs: Open LoloBuy's official shipping estimator and select the Netherlands as the destination. Enter the requested weight, dimensions and goods category using the units shown by the current form. Check grams against kilograms before comparing results. A weight entered in the wrong unit describes a different parcel, even if the resulting screen looks plausible. Save the inputs together with the displayed options.

For each eligible route, record the quotation date, currency, quoted amount, estimated transit period, tracking information and stated restrictions. Keep the contents and measurements identical while comparing routes. If a route requires a different packing method, note that difference explicitly. Do not turn an old screenshot into a current price table. A useful comparison can be repeated with measured warehouse data when that information becomes available.

sections.heading: Understand what a lighter or smaller carton changes
paragraphs: Actual weight measures mass; volumetric weight represents the space the parcel occupies under a route's billing rule. LoloBuy's weight guidance describes route-dependent formulas. Read the current conditions rather than applying one divisor to every service. Also check rounding, minimum charges and the increment used for additional weight. Reducing the physical weight slightly may leave the parcel in the same price band.

Consider an illustrative carton measuring 40 by 30 by 20 centimetres. Its volume is 24,000 cubic centimetres. With a hypothetical divisor of 6,000, dimensional weight would be 4 kilograms. Reducing one side to 15 centimetres would produce 3 kilograms under that same assumed rule. This calculation explains a packing comparison; it does not establish an available LoloBuy route, a freight price or a guaranteed saving.

sections.heading: Compare consolidation with separate parcels
paragraphs: When several items are in storage, compare one combined parcel with the total for all proposed separate parcels. Use the same destination and include the packing services for each option. A smaller amount shown beside one split parcel is not the total cost of shipping the whole basket. Each parcel can have its own minimum charge and separate destination processing.

Protection and restrictions can matter more than the lowest initial freight. A fragile item may need separation or reinforcement, while a bulky box may dominate the volume of an otherwise compact parcel. Ask for the particular arrangement you want considered. Keep necessary protection and check that the selected service accepts the actual contents. Consolidation is a decision to evaluate, not an automatic promise of lower cost.

sections.heading: Read delivery time as a sequence
paragraphs: Separate seller dispatch, delivery to the Chinese warehouse, inspection, parcel preparation, international transport, destination processing and final delivery. A carrier transit estimate may cover only part of that sequence. Record the milestone from which an estimate starts before comparing it with another shopper's total wait. Order confirmation and carrier acceptance are not the same starting event.

After dispatch, follow the parcel reference in the account and the carrier information associated with it. A created tracking number does not by itself establish that the carrier has physically accepted the parcel. When progress is unclear, ask which milestone has been completed and which party holds the parcel. For a time-sensitive purchase, leave a buffer instead of treating an estimated arrival window as a guaranteed date.

sections.heading: Check current Dutch import information
paragraphs: Before payment, consult Dutch Customs' current information for online purchases arriving from outside the European Union. Its guidance distinguishes VAT, import duty and carrier handling costs. The rules for low-value consignments changed in July 2026, so an older guide saying that a low-value purchase is automatically free of import duty should not be used as a current calculation. Check the rules applicable to the actual goods and import date.

Keep the item descriptions, purchase amounts, currency and any tax or duty already collected together. Ask the carrier or seller how an included charge is documented and what remains payable. A shipping-line nickname does not establish the tax treatment of your parcel. This guide does not calculate a universal Dutch customs bill: product classification, the transaction and the applicable procedure matter. Use accurate descriptions and values when providing the requested information.

sections.heading: Reconcile the final freight and retain evidence
paragraphs: The official LoloBuy freight guidance describes collecting an estimate and later reconciling it with the logistics charge. Compare any adjustment with the final packed weight, dimensions, route and selected services. If the amount changes, identify the changed input before assuming the estimate was a fixed commitment. Keep the initial quotation and the final parcel bill in the same record.

When delivery arrives, compare the contents with the saved item list and inspect the packaging before discarding it. Preserve photographs if something appears missing or damaged, then use the order or parcel support process relevant to the issue. Seller returns, international parcel claims and carrier charges involve different records. Good documentation makes the request clearer without promising a particular refund or resolution.

sections.heading: Build a useful record for the next order
paragraphs: After completing an order, retain what can be compared honestly: the date, destination, actual goods, measured carton, selected service, final freight and the observed delivery milestones. Remove personal address information before sharing an example. A historical shipment can help another buyer understand the process, but it should remain labelled as one dated case rather than a general price or delivery promise.

Use that record to improve the next estimate. Note whether volume or weight controlled the charge, whether an optional service changed the carton, and which budget item was initially overlooked. Before reusing the figures, check that the destination, contents and current route conditions still match. A repeatable method is more useful than collecting the cheapest-looking number from a different parcel.

checklist: Select the Netherlands and the correct postcode in the current quote.
Save identical weight, volume and contents for route comparisons.
Separate warehouse time, international transit and final delivery.
Verify current Dutch import guidance and any amount already collected.
Keep initial and final parcel bills together.

articles.title: LoloBuy payment methods and fees: checkout, currency and balance
articles.description: Check LoloBuy payment methods at checkout, compare the complete debit, and distinguish account balance credits from refunds to the original payment method.
articles.summary: Match every payment to an item order or parcel bill. Compare the current total and currency, keep the transaction reference, and verify where any refund is credited.

sections.heading: Begin with the bill you intend to pay
paragraphs: Before choosing a payment method, identify the subject of the bill. It may concern a product order, domestic delivery, international freight, an adjustment or an account top-up. The official LoloBuy purchase process separates the goods payment from the later parcel payment. A successful first transaction does not establish that every later stage of the purchase is already paid.

Keep the order or parcel number, amount and currency beside the payment screen. If several bills have similar totals, use their references rather than the amount alone to distinguish them. Confirm that the selected items and quantities are correct before comparing payment channels.
